fields.h1: Build Yearbook Survey Questions and Collect Every Answer
fields.hero_description: Build yearbook survey questions that take one answer per student and keep every answer in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Yearbook Survey
fields.features_subheading: Yearbook survey questions gather the quotes, votes, and memories for student pages. Emergent builds the survey and its table.
fields.feature_1:
Questions grouped by yearbook page

Name the pages the survey feeds, such as superlatives, senior quotes, and the class page. Emergent drafts a section of questions for each one, and you change any question by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
One answer per student on the roster

Load the class roster, and the survey takes one answer per student ID. Students answer one question per screen on a phone, and a second try opens the answers they already sent.
fields.feature_3:
Superlatives counted by category

The app counts nominations in each superlative category as they arrive. A tie stays marked on the editors' view until a runoff settles it, then the winner moves to the page list.
fields.feature_4:
Character limits on quotes and memories

Set a limit on senior quotes and memory answers. A student who types past it sees the count turn red and trims the quote before sending it, rather than after the spread is laid out.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders before the deadline

Students who have not answered get an email reminder before the deadline. The adviser gets a Slack list of who is still missing by homeroom, and finished students hear nothing.
fields.feature_6:
A database and code that stay yours

Each answer is a row in a database you own, tagged with name and homeroom. Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. The free tier covers building and publishing.
fields.why_title: Why Build Your Yearbook Survey on Emergent?
fields.why_description: Next year's staff should start from this year's survey. Every question and every answer stays in a database you own.

plan.angle: The top 10 is printable question sheets, Pinterest pins and personality quizzes: lists of prompts with nothing to collect, count or chase the answers. This page shows a yearbook adviser, a senior class, an elementary teacher and a middle school staff running yearbook survey questions as an app: one answer per student checked against the roster, superlative votes tallied per category, quotes held to a length limit, and every answer in a table the editors lay out from.
tab_stories: Wexley High's yearbook staff asks 286 seniors to nominate classmates in 12 superlative categories, the app counts one ballot per student against the roster, 241 of 286 answer, and a 31 to 31 tie for Best Laugh goes to a runoff.

Corvallen Academy's 148 seniors each send a quote of up to 120 characters, the adviser approves or returns each one, and 9 days before the page deadline the app emails the 22 who still have not answered.

Ellery Park Elementary's third-grade teacher sends a 6-question All About Me survey to the families of 24 students, and the class page prints one row per child, with 7 of 24 naming a veterinarian as their future job.
Tarrant Hill Middle School's yearbook club polls 488 students on the year's trends in 5 questions, the results split by grade, and the top song for 8th grade takes the trends spread with 112 votes.
